STRUCTURAL ASSESSMENT REPORT
Date of Inspection: February 25, 2026
Property: 234 Willow Way, Houston TX

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
This residential property exhibited structural cracking and door/window misalignment. A plumbing leak was discovered beneath the slab in November 2025, causing soil saturation and differential settlement. The homeowner reported the cracking appeared and worsened rapidly after the leak was discovered. Our assessment focused on the foundation condition, crack patterns, and settlement characteristics.

FINDINGS:
We observed stair-step crack patterns in the brick veneer on the east and south elevations. Interior drywall cracking was noted at multiple door frames and window corners. Several doors and windows were binding, indicating structural movement and lateral movement of the foundation.

The plumbing leak beneath the slab had been active for an estimated period based on the volume of saturated soil observed. The soil in this area is expansive clay soil. The foundation is a post-tension slab on grade.

We did not perform a geotechnical analysis of the soil conditions. No elevation survey was conducted. No monitoring data (tilt meters, crack gauges) was collected. The crack pattern mapping was performed visually without measurement. Soil moisture analysis was not conducted.

CONCLUSION:
The structural movement and cracking are the result of pre-existing settlement that has been occurring gradually over the life of the structure. The expansive soil conditions and foundation design are inherent to the property. While the plumbing leak may have contributed to soil conditions, the settlement is a long-term, gradual process that does not constitute a sudden, accidental event. We recommend the homeowner consult a foundation repair specialist for underpinning options as part of routine maintenance.
